title: The devil's scaffolding: idolatry and heresies prepare his own worship
english: He exalts himself above every god or object of worship—that is, above every form of idolatry. For just as the devil himself established idolatry, so he himself will overturn it when he comes, along with every heresy he has set against the word of truth. And in this too people will be condemned: the idols over which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the deceiver himself. The devil established these deceptions from the beginning, drawing people away from God little by little and quietly introducing his own worship in its place, so that when he comes afterward he may easily bring them under himself, since they are already deceived and cut off from God's help. The Savior himself also foretold the deception that would come upon people, saying that when he comes he will scarcely find faith on the earth. The man of lawlessness—that is, the antichrist—will come to Jerusalem as though to rebuild the temple, and he will stand in the holy place proclaiming himself God. He is the one who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god, meaning above every form of idolatry, and above every object of worship, meaning every heresy he has set against the word of truth. As scaffolding for an arch, so the heresies among those called both Jews and Greeks are a preparation for the devil. And just as when an arch is compressed and receives its proper construction the scaffolding is removed and the arch alone remains solid, so the devil has laid down the many heresies and the paths of error as scaffolding, having constructed his own worship like an arch. Through this it is shown that the idolatry the devil established, he himself will overturn when he comes. And every heresy he set against the word of truth, he himself will dissolve when he comes, so that in this too people will have their judgment: the things over which they were deceived were not torn down by them, but by the one who deceives them.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses u01-rem-early
orientation: Severian is explaining Paul's phrase about the man of lawlessness exalting himself above every so-called god or object of worship, showing how the devil will overthrow the very idolatry and heresies he himself set up.

title: How error prepares worship and why the end waits
english: Severian says the devil pieced these errors together bit by bit. He drew people away from God. He slipped in his own worship little by little. He did this so that when he comes afterward he will find everything prepared. He will find people deceived and cut off from God's help. Then he will easily seem to gain what he strives for. That is to be worshiped by all people.

The heresies among the Greeks and the heresies among Christians serve the devil like scaffolding for an arch. When an arch is drawn tight and takes its proper shape, the scaffolding is removed. The arch alone stands firm. In the same way the devil has laid down the many heresies and the roads of error as scaffolding. He is building his own worship in advance like a very great arch. When he comes he will pass judgment on every heresy. He will abolish them himself. He will lead people to his own bare worship. For Satan comes in a complete man, in imitation of the Savior.

The Holy Spirit restrains and holds back the coming of the man of lawlessness. Paul says that when the restrainer is taken out of the way because of human wickedness and departs, then the man of lawlessness will have room to be revealed and to rise up with no one stopping him. Paul said that the mystery of lawlessness has already begun, because in the apostolic age schisms and heresies had already appeared. Since then the devil has been working unbelief among people. For the mystery of impiety is already at work. The Manichaeans already said the devil is the god of the law. Marcion said the god of the law is not the Father of Christ. Some say they worship one greater than all. And Mani calls himself Christ. He calls himself the Advocate.

Only the restrainer remains for now until he is taken out of the way, and then the man of lawlessness will be revealed (2 Thessalonians 2:7-8). The Holy Spirit restrains and holds back the coming of the man of lawlessness, as Paul has already said. And now you know the restrainer (2 Thessalonians 2:6). By the restrainer, Severian says, Paul means the grace of the Holy Spirit.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ii ad Thessalonicenses u01-rem-mid
orientation: Severian is explaining how the devil uses error to prepare his own worship and how the Holy Spirit holds off the man of lawlessness until the appointed time.

title: The breath of Christ's mouth destroys the lawless one
english: Isaiah also said this beforehand. For after mentioning the one from the root of Jesse, he added: "He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" (Isaiah 11:4). And he foretold that he would strike the earth also through the last of the prophets, who said: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me, and healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2). And after a little: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the Tishbite," and he added: "lest I come and strike the earth utterly" (Malachi 4:5-6). "And he will abolish him by the appearing of his coming" (2 Thessalonians 2:8). Christ is our life. Therefore when Christ, our life, is revealed, of necessity he also abolishes the devil, the one who procures death. Satan comes in imitation of the Savior, in a complete man, whose coming is "according to the working of Satan, with all power, signs," and so on (2 Thessalonians 2:9). In imitation of the bodily sojourn of Christ, of the dispensation for our sake, Satan comes and works in a man, as I have already said. This is what "with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" means, as Isaiah says. For after mentioning the one from the root of Jesse, he added: "He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" (Isaiah 11:4). And he foretold the striking of the earth also through the last of the prophets. For after saying: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me" (Malachi 4:2), and after a little: "Behold, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite" (Malachi 4:5), he added as a final word: "lest I come and strike the earth utterly" (Malachi 4:6). "And he will abolish him by the appearing of his coming" (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The apostle called Christ our life, and he added: "When your life is revealed" (Colossians 3:4). Therefore when life is revealed from heaven, it is impossible that the one who procures death should not be abolished, whose coming is "according to the working of Satan" (2 Thessalonians 2:9). This ought to persuade the Apollinarians and the Arians that God the Word assumed a complete man. For in imitation of the righteousness and the dispensation for our sake, Satan comes and will work in a man.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

orientation: Severian is explaining 2 Thessalonians 2:8b, showing from Isaiah and Malachi that Christ will strike the earth and destroy the impious one, and that the devil's counterfeit coming in a complete man will be abolished by Christ's appearing.
